entries.9adaca89eb314ffd7972bc68a3684ce433142c69: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11788"/><div sID="gen21341" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11788"/>4-5. (Compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.17-Ezek.39.20">Eze 39:17-20</reference>).<div eID="gen21341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21342" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">upon the mountains of Israel--</hi>The scene of Israel's preservation shall be that of the ungodly foe's destruction. <div eID="gen21342" type="x-p"/>
entries.01d93c6cb5cd9917a7e97676ffc65331a51f5ad3: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11789"/><div sID="gen21343" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11789"/><hi type="bold">6. carelessly--</hi>in self-confident security.<div eID="gen21343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21344" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the isles--</hi>Those dwelling in maritime regions, who had helped Gog with fleets and troops, shall be visited with the fire of God's wrath in their own lands. <div eID="gen21344" type="x-p"/>
entries.ddc9ae9db01f3f93abd47688fc8e9fbe79e4c318: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11790"/><div sID="gen21345" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11790"/><hi type="bold">7. not let them pollute my holy name--</hi>by their sins bringing down judgments which made the heathen think that I was unable or unwilling to save My people. <div eID="gen21345" type="x-p"/>
entries.e39dc231c7fb2d88f8b1b0bfdf4ad05623af9aa7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11791"/><div sID="gen21346" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11791"/><hi type="bold">8. it is come ... it is done--</hi>The prediction of the salvation of My people, and the ruin of their enemy, is come to pass--is done: expressing that the event foretold is as certain as if it were already accomplished. <div eID="gen21346" type="x-p"/>
entries.481abf8fb2c920fdb20148977779c6346a67f2ef: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11792"/><div sID="gen21347" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11792"/>9-10. The burning of the foe's weapons implies that nothing belonging to them should be left to pollute the land. The seven years (seven being the sacred number) spent on this work, implies the completeness of the cleansing, and the people's zeal for purity. How different from the ancient Israelites, who left not merely the arms, but the heathen themselves, to remain among them [Fairbairn], (<reference osisRef="Judg.1.27">Jud 1:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.28">28</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.3">2:2, 3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.106.34-Ps.106.36">Psa 106:34-36</reference>). The desolation by Antiochus began in the one hundred and forty-first year of the Seleucidæ. From this date to 148, a period of six years and four months ("2300 days," <reference osisRef="Dan.8.14">Da 8:14</reference>), when the temple-worship was restored (1 Maccabees 4:52), God vouchsafed many triumphs to His people; from this time to the death of Antiochus, early in 149, a period of seven months, the Jews had rest from Antiochus, and purified their land, and on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month celebrated the Encænia, or feast of dedication (<reference osisRef="John.10.22">Joh 10:22</reference>) and purification of the temple. The whole period, in round numbers, was seven years. Mattathias was the patriotic Jewish leader, and his third son, Judas, the military commander under whom the Syrian generals were defeated. He retook Jerusalem and purified the temple. Simon and Jonathan, his brothers, succeeded him: the independence of the Jews was secured, and the crown vested in the Asmonean family, in which it continued till Herod the Great. <div eID="gen21347" type="x-p"/>
entries.9118c415eaf01eaa07707eeb9a37b4492b7b9bca: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11793"/><div sID="gen21348" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11793"/><hi type="bold">11. place ... of graves--</hi>Gog found only a grave where he had expected the spoils of conquest.<div eID="gen21348" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21349" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">valley--</hi>So vast were to be the masses that nothing but a deep valley would suffice for their corpses.<div eID="gen21349" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21350" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the passengers on the east of the sea--</hi>those travelling on the high road, east of the Dead Sea, from Syria to Petra and Egypt. The publicity of the road would cause many to observe God's judgments, as the stench (as English Version translates) or the multitude of graves (as Henderson translates, "it shall stop the passengers") would arrest the attention of passers-by. Their grave would be close to that of their ancient prototypes, Sodom and Gomorrah in the Dead Sea, both alike being signal instances of God's judgments. <div eID="gen21350" type="x-p"/>
entries.7b62d0ee885ce7012e6b37e51338c6313702814f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11794"/><div sID="gen21351" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11794"/><hi type="bold">13. I ... glorified--</hi>in destroying the foe (<reference osisRef="Ezek.28.22">Eze 28:22</reference>). <div eID="gen21351" type="x-p"/>
entries.995d9e2cea3b18e64e5f671af385ae6a42385717: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11795"/><div sID="gen21352" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11795"/><hi type="bold">14. with the passengers--</hi>The men employed continually in the burying were to be helped by those happening to pass by; all were to combine.<div eID="gen21352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21353" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">after the end of seven months shall they search--</hi>to see if the work was complete [Munster]. <div eID="gen21353" type="x-p"/>
entries.34300365304b24f76a6ec4dae4f0e5ace8c8ac02: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11796"/><div sID="gen21354" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11796"/>15. First "all the people of the land" engaged in the burying for seven months; then special men were employed, at the end of the seven months, to search for any still left unburied. The passers-by helped them by setting up a mark near any such bones, in order to keep others from being defiled by casually touching them, and that the buriers might come and remove them. Denoting the minute care to put away every relic of heathen pollution from the Holy Land. <div eID="gen21354" type="x-p"/>
entries.d0caa9f52035200465fe74f81414ec996b568760: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11797"/><div sID="gen21355" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11797"/>16. A city in the neighborhood was to receive the name Hamonah, "multitude," to commemorate the overthrow of the multitudes of the foe [Henderson]. The multitude of the slain shall give a name to the city of Jerusalem after the land shall have been cleansed [Grotius]. Jerusalem shall be famed as the conqueror of multitudes. <div eID="gen21355" type="x-p"/>
entries.6c3253794c2af76730bbfba66ede3624cfc35e53: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11798"/><div sID="gen21356" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11798"/>17. (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.17">Re 19:17</reference>).<div eID="gen21356" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21357" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sacrifice--</hi>Anciently worshippers feasted on the sacrifices. The birds and beasts of prey are invited to the sacrificial feast provided by God (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.18.6">Is 18:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.34.6">34:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.1.7">Zep 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mark.9.49">Mr 9:49</reference>). Here this sacrifice holds only a subordinate place in the picture, and so is put last. Not only shall their bones lie long unburied, but they shall be stripped of the flesh by beasts and birds of prey. <div eID="gen21357" type="x-p"/>
entries.ec55372e6f9eea730ebd54a724b3bd33649df53f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11799"/><div sID="gen21358" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11799"/><hi type="bold">18. rams ... lambs ... goats--</hi>By these various animal victims used in sacrifices are meant various ranks of men, princes, generals, and soldiers (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.34.6">Is 34:6</reference>).<div eID="gen21358" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21359" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fatlings of Bashan--</hi>ungodly men of might (<reference osisRef="Ps.22.12">Psa 22:12</reference>). Bashan, beyond Jordan, was famed for its fat cattle. Fat implies prosperity which often makes men refractory towards God (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.14">De 32:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.32.15">15</reference>). <div eID="gen21359" type="x-p"/>
entries.8924368d06bd05064cb6feb52b3c26ff9482bab1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11800"/><div sID="gen21360" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11800"/><hi type="bold">20. my table--</hi>the field of battle on the mountains of Israel (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.8">Eze 38:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.20">20</reference>).<div eID="gen21360" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21361" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">chariots--</hi>that is, charioteers. <div eID="gen21361" type="x-p"/>
entries.8e33501b0f410be5e1ba893860215848fdaae25b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11801"/><div sID="gen21362" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11801"/><hi type="bold">22. So the house of Israel shall know ... Lord--</hi>by My interposition for them. So, too, the heathen shall be led to fear the name of the Lord (<reference osisRef="Ps.102.15">Psa 102:15</reference>). <div eID="gen21362" type="x-p"/>
entries.5ca1f75b2e92faaec101de587a5cfc36b67a7d24: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11802"/><div sID="gen21363" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11802"/><hi type="bold">23. hid I my face--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Deut.31.17">De 31:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.59.2">Is 59:2</reference>). <div eID="gen21363" type="x-p"/>
entries.476f389226ff655ea77e5989ad27d3711fdff78c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11803"/><div sID="gen21364" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11803"/><hi type="bold">25. bring again the captivity--</hi>restore from calamity to prosperity.<div eID="gen21364" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21365" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the whole house of Israel--</hi>so "all Israel" (<reference osisRef="Rom.11.26">Ro 11:26</reference>). The restorations of Israel heretofore have been partial; there must be one yet future that is to be universal (<reference osisRef="Hos.1.11">Ho 1:11</reference>). <div eID="gen21365" type="x-p"/>
entries.f7504d30bfbc84515214511e136487c359d7a4fd: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11804"/><div sID="gen21366" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11804"/><hi type="bold">26. After that they have borne their shame--</hi>the punishment of their sin: after they have become sensible of their guilt, and ashamed of it (<reference osisRef="Ezek.20.43">Eze 20:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.31">36:31</reference>). <div eID="gen21366" type="x-p"/>
entries.16ce6135241d654d4daf2719198f622c8e5d786c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11805"/><div sID="gen21367" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11805"/><hi type="bold">27. sanctified in them--</hi>vindicated as holy in My dealings with them. <div eID="gen21367" type="x-p"/>
entries.3328c28081194629a7abd12b0f271f5a84fce399: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11806"/><div sID="gen21368" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11806"/>28. The Jews, having no dominion, settled country, or fixed property to detain them, may return at any time without difficulty (compare <reference osisRef="Hos.3.4">Ho 3:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.3.5">5</reference>). <div eID="gen21368" type="x-p"/>
entries.b533862338efd11a5e74c245ce1b9e224c58b026: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11807"/><div sID="gen21369" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11807"/><hi type="bold">29. poured out my Spirit upon ... Israel--</hi>the sure forerunner of their conversion (<reference osisRef="Joel.2.28">Joe 2:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zec 12:10</reference>). The pouring out of His Spirit is a pledge that He will hide His face no more (<reference osisRef="2Cor.1.22">2Co 1:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.1.14">Ep 1:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.1.6">Php 1:6</reference>). <chapter eID="Ezek.39"/>

entries.bd6e71035533cba0602185206c94e4fd1270497b: <div eID="gen32447" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen32448" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32449" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32449" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen32448" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen32450" type="x-p"/> The prophet goes on to denounce the Divine judgments against Gog and his army, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.1-Eze.39.7">Eze 39:1-7</reference>; and describes their dreadful slaughter, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.8-Eze.39.10">Eze 39:8-10</reference>, and burial, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.11-Eze.39.16">Eze 39:11-16</reference>, in terms so very lofty and comprehensive, as must certainly denote some very extraordinary interposition of Providence in behalf of the Jews. And to amplify the matter still more, the prophet, with peculiar art and propriety, delays the summoning of all the birds and beasts of prey in nature to feast on the slain, (in allusion to the custom of feasting on the remainder of sacrifices), till after the greater multitudes are buried; to intimate that even the remainder, and as it were the stragglers of such mighty hosts, would be more than sufficient to satisfy their utmost rapacity, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.17-Eze.39.20">Eze 39:17-20</reference>. The remaining verses contain a prediction of the great blessedness of the people of God in Gospel times, and of the stability of the kingdom of Christ, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.21-Eze.39.29">Eze 39:21-29</reference>. It will be proper to remark that the great northern expedition against the natural Israel, described in this and the preceding chapter, is, from its striking resemblance in the main particulars, put by the writer of the Apocalypse, (<reference osisRef="Eze.20.7-Eze.20.10">Eze 20:7-10</reference>), for a much more formidable armament of a multitude of nations in the four quarters of the earth against the pure Christian Church, the Mystical Israel; an event still extremely remote, and which it is thought shall immediately precede the destruction of the world by fire, and the general judgment.
entries.2bca20ab55963e08721f14ecbb2065e857b33f7e: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen32450" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32451" type="x-p"/> And leave but the sixth part of thee - The margin has, strike thee with six plagues; or, draw thee back with a hook of six teeth.
entries.0d62f2184e0dd6a62091fa0bc7527c1c37f0d6ab: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen32451" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32452" type="x-p"/> I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand - The Persians whom Antiochus had in his army, <reference osisRef="Eze.38.5">Eze 38:5</reference>, were famous as archers, and they may be intended here. The bow is held by the left hand; the arrow is pulled and discharged by the right.
entries.74097dd76bb2c8ddab75b5d1b3b2d63860a5aab3: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen32452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32453" type="x-p"/> I will send a fire on Magog - On Syria. I will destroy the Syrian troops. <div eID="gen32453" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32454" type="x-p"/> And among them that dwell carelessly in the isles - The auxiliary troops that came to Antiochus from the borders of the Euxine Sea. - Martin.
entries.1e529ac7c3e0c11ae1afd4d4dfd53fac94f3dacb: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen32454" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32455" type="x-p"/> In the midst of my people Israel - This defeat of Gog is to be in Israel: and it was there according to this prophecy, that the immense army of Antiochus was so completely defeated. <div eID="gen32455" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32456" type="x-p"/> Ands I will not let them pollute my holy name any more - See on 1 Maccabees 1:11, etc., how Antiochus had profaned the temple, insulted Jehovah and his worship, etc. God permitted that as a scourge to his disobedient people; but now the scourger shall be scourged, and he shall pollute the sanctuary no more.
entries.972aff8bf7799a7d653fc0d00d2b647acc00902b: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen32456" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32457" type="x-p"/> And shall set on fire - the weapons - The Israelites shall make bonfires and fuel of the weapons, tents, etc., which the defeated Syrians shall leave behind them, as expressive of the joy which they shall feel for the destruction of their enemies; and to keep up, in their culinary consumption, the memory of this great event. <div eID="gen32457" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32458" type="x-p"/> They shall burn them with fire seven years - These may be figurative expressions, after the manner of the Asiatics, whose language abounds with such descriptions. They occur every where in the prophets. As to the number seven it is only a certain for an indeterminate number. But as the slaughter was great, and the bows, arrows, quivers, shields, bucklers, handstaves, and spears were in vast multitudes, it must have taken a long time to gather them up in the different parts of the fields of battle, and the roads in which the Syrians had retreated, throwing away their arms as they proceeded; so there might have been a long time employed in collecting and burning them. And as all seem to have been doomed to the fire, there might have been some found at different intervals and burned, during the seven years here mentioned. Mariana, in his History of Spain, lib. xi., c. 24, says, that after the Spaniards had given that signal overthrow to the Saracens, a.d. 1212 they found such a vast quantity of lances, javelins, and such like, that they served them for four years for fuel. And probably these instruments obtained by the Israelites were used in general for culinary firewood, and might literally have served them for seven years; so that during that time they should take no wood out of the fields, nor out of the forests for the purpose of fuel, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.10">Eze 39:10</reference>.
entries.5c1d771877d555f9adfc1b8a2b68eb4081f2acdb: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen32458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32459" type="x-p"/> The valley of the passengers on the east of the sea - That is, of Gennesareth, according to the Targum. The valley near this lake or sea is called the Valley of the Passengers, because it was a great road by which the merchants and traders from Syria and other eastern countries went into Egypt; see <reference osisRef="Gen.37.17">Gen 37:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.37.25">Gen 37:25</reference>. See Calmet here. <div eID="gen32459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32460" type="x-p"/> There shall they bury Gog and all his multitude - Some read, "There shall they bury Gog, that is, all his multitude." Not Gog, or Antiochus himself, for he was not in this battle; but his generals, captains, and soldiers, by whom he was represented. As to Hamon-gog, we know no valley of this name but here. But we may understand the words thus: the place where this great slaughter was, and where the multitudes of the slain were buried, might be better called Hamon-gog, the valley of the multitude of God, than the valley of passengers; for so great was the carnage there, that the way of the passengers shall be stopped by it. See the text.
entries.62f77197ff980fc75baec313c6c61430c7ad000d: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen32460" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32461" type="x-p"/> And seven months - It shall require a long time to bury the dead. This is another figurative expression; which, however, may admit of a good deal of literal meaning. Many of the Syrian soldiers had secreted themselves in different places during the pursuit after the battle, where they died of their wounds, of hunger, and of fatigue; so that they were not all found and buried till seven months after the defeat of the Syrian army. This slow process of burying is distinctly related in the three following verses, and extended even to a bone, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.15">Eze 39:15</reference>; which, when it was found by a passenger, the place was marked, that the buriers might see and inter it. Seven months was little time enough for all this work; and in that country putrescency does not easily take place: the scorching winds serving to desiccate the flesh, and preserve it from decomposition.
entries.b71be1e5232275d8595870f80d2aa5b700449066: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen32461" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32462" type="x-p"/> Gather yourselves - to my sacrifice - This is an allusion to a custom common in the east: when a sacrifice is made, the friends and neighbors of the party sacrificing are invited to come and feast on the sacrifice.
entries.7d2196768ed20ff56c46f565759369727f320fe9: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen32462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32463" type="x-p"/> Ye shall - drink the blood of the princes of the earth - I need not mention the custom of the Scandinavians: they were accustomed to drink the blood of their enemies out of the skulls of the dead. But this is spoken of fowls and beasts here - rams, lambs, and goats. The feast shall be as grateful and as plenteous to the fowls and beasts, as one made of the above animals, the fattest and best of their kind, (because fed in the fertile fields of Bashan), would be to the guests of him who makes a sacrifice.
entries.0a75e365c8f45f8f88ab3fe5f1e61b23c6bafd05: <hi type="bold">Verse 19</hi> <div eID="gen32463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32464" type="x-p"/> And ye shall eat fat - and drink blood - Who shall eat and drink, etc.? Not the Jews: though Voltaire says they ate human flesh, and are invited here by the prophet to eat the flesh and drink the blood of their enemies; which is a most unprincipled falsehood. It is the fowls and the beasts that God invites, <reference osisRef="Eze.39.17">Eze 39:17</reference> : "Speak to every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, assemble yourselves - that ye may eat flesh and drink blood;" nor are the persons altered in all these <reference osisRef="Eze.39.17-Eze.39.20">Eze 39:17-20</reference> : so the assertion of Voltaire is either through brutish ignorance or Satanic malice.
entries.551432cfc4d4c60b1a6f443207aaee9723b9a105: <hi type="bold">Verse 25</hi> <div eID="gen32464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32465" type="x-p"/> Now will I bring again the captivity of Jacob - Both they and the heathen shall know that it was for their iniquity that I gave them into the hands of their enemies: and now I will redeem them from those hands in such a way as to prove that I am a merciful God, as well as a just God.
entries.2f4e9b15f11b2cb09092ac9884e34a0c77a7a2e3: <hi type="bold">Verse 26</hi> <div eID="gen32465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32466" type="x-p"/> After that they have borne their shame - After they shall have borne the punishment due to a line of conduct which is their shame and reproach, viz. idolatry.
entries.97edfbe500ab81d57c8542400c130aef2f0d4993: <hi type="bold">Verse 27</hi> <div eID="gen32466" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32467" type="x-p"/> When I have - gathered them - Antiochus had before captured many of the Jews, and sold them for slaves; see <reference osisRef="Dan.11.33">Dan 11:33</reference>.
entries.982371cc49d2a327837e5cb84ca533218a7ca821: <hi type="bold">Verse 28</hi> <div eID="gen32467" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32468" type="x-p"/> And have left none of then any more there - All that chose had liberty to return; but many remained behind. This promise may therefore refer to a greater restoration, when not a Jew shall be left behind. This, the next verse intimates, will be in the Gospel dispensation.
entries.e5170b18098c7267d93ec6ce8840561186f44bc9: <hi type="bold">Verse 29</hi> <div eID="gen32468" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32469" type="x-p"/> For I have poured out my Spirit - That is, I will pour out my Spirit; see the notes on <reference osisRef="Eze.36.25-Eze.36.29">Eze 36:25-29</reference> (note), where this subject is largely considered. This Spirit is to enlighten, quicken, purify, and cleanse their hearts; so that, being completely changed, they shall become God's people, and be a praise in the earth. Now, they are a proverb of reproach; then, they shall be eminently distinguished.  <chapter eID="Ezek.39"/> <div eID="gen32469" type="x-p"/>

entries.50ceab6a5bd5d2d2a46d9997a55a2f198e264f98: <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.1-Ezek.39.8">Eze 39:1-8</reference> <div eID="gen15199" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">Further Description of the Judgment to Fall upon Gog and his Hosts</title> <div sID="gen15200" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.1">Eze 39:1</reference>-8. General announcement of his destruction. - Eze 39:1. <hi type="italic">And thou, son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Behold, I will deal with thee, Gog, thou prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.</hi> Eze 39:2. <hi type="italic">I will mislead thee, and conduct thee, and cause thee to come up from the uttermost north, and bring thee to the mountains of Israel;</hi> Eze 39:3. <hi type="italic">And will smite thy bow from thy left hand, and cause thine arrows to fall from thy right hand.</hi> Eze 39:4. <hi type="italic">Upon the mountains of Israel wilt thou fall, thou and all thy hosts, and the peoples which are with thee: I give thee for food to the birds of prey of every plumage, and to the beasts of the field.</hi> Eze 39:5. <hi type="italic">Upon the open field shalt thou fall, for I have spoken it, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah.</hi> Eze 39:6. <hi type="italic">And I will send fire in Magog, and among those who dwell in security upon the islands, that they may know that I am Jehovah.</hi> Eze 39:7. <hi type="italic">I will make known my holy name in the midst of my people Israel, and will not let my holy name be profaned any more, that the nations may know that I am Jehovah, holy in Israel.</hi> Eze 39:8. <hi type="italic">Behold, it comes and happens, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah; this is the day of which I spoke.</hi> - The further description of the judgment with which Gog and his hosts are threatened in <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.21-Ezek.38.23">Eze 38:21-23</reference>, commences with a repetition of the command to the prophet to prophesy against Gog (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.1">Eze 39:1</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.2-Ezek.38.3">Eze 38:2-3</reference>). The principal contents of <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.4-Ezek.38.15">Eze 38:4-15</reference> are then briefly summed up in Eze 39:2. שׁבבתּיך, as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.4">Eze 38:4</reference>, is strengthened by שׁשּׁתיך, שׁשׁא, ἁπαχ λεγ.., is not connected with שׁשׁ in the sense of “I leave a sixth part of thee remaining,” or afflict thee with six punishments; but in the Ethiopic it signifies to proceed, or to climb, and here, accordingly, it is used in the sense of leading on (lxx καθοδηγήσω σε, or, according to another reading, κατάξω; Vulg. <hi type="italic">educam</hi>). For <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Ezek.39.2">Eze 39:2</reference></hi>, compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.15">Eze 38:15</reference> and Eze 38:8. In the land of Israel, God will strike his weapons out of his hands, i.e., make him incapable of fighting (for the fact itself, compare the similar figures in <reference osisRef="Ps.37.15">Psa 37:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.46.10">Psa 46:10</reference>), and give him up with all his army as a prey to death. עיט, a beast of prey, is more precisely defined by צפּור, and still further strengthened by the genitive כּל־כּנף: birds of prey of every kind. The judgment will not be confined to the destruction of the army of Gog, which has invaded the land of Israel, but (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.6">Eze 39:6</reference>) will also extend to the land of Gog, and to all the heathen nations that are dwelling in security. אשׁ, fire, primarily the fire of war; then, in a further sense, a figure denoting destruction inflicted directly by God, as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.22">Eze 38:22</reference>, which is therefore represented in <reference osisRef="Rev.20.9">Rev 20:9</reference> as fire falling from heaven. <hi type="italic">Magog</hi> is the population of the land of Magog (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.2">Eze 38:2</reference>). With this the inhabitants of the distant coastlands of the west (the איּים) are associated, as representatives of the remotest heathen nations. <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.7">Eze 39:7</reference>, Eze 39:8. By this judgment the Lord will make known His holy name in Israel, and show the heathen that He will not let it be blasphemed by them any more. For the fact itself, compare Eze 36:20. For <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.8">Eze 39:8</reference>, compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.12">Eze 21:12</reference>, and for היּום, see <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.18">Eze 38:18</reference>-19.
entries.5b961d3b99f38d177910a26d4ef586bbd9334e40: <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.9-Ezek.39.20">Eze 39:9-20</reference> <div eID="gen15200" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">Total Destruction of Gog and his Hosts</title> <div sID="gen15201" type="x-p"/> Eze 39:9. <hi type="italic">Then will the inhabitants of the cities of Israel go forth, and burn and heat with armour and shield and target, with bow and arrows and hand-staves and spears, and will burn fire with them for seven years;</hi> Eze 39:10. <hi type="italic">And will not fetch wood from the field, nor cut wood out of the forests, but will burn fire with the armour, and will spoil those who spoiled them, and plunder those who plundered them, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah.</hi> Eze 39:11. <hi type="italic">And it will come to pass in that day, that I will give Gog a place where his grave in Israel shall be, the valley of the travellers, and there will they bury Gog and all his multitude, and will call it the valley of Gog’s multitude.</hi> Eze 39:12. <hi type="italic">They of the house of Israel will bury them, to purify the land for seven months. V.1 3. And all the people of the land will bury, and it will be to them for a name on the day when I glorify myself, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah.</hi> Eze 39:14. <hi type="italic">And they will set apart constant men, such as rove about in the land, and such as bury with them that rove about those who remain upon the surface of the ground, to cleanse it, after the lapse of seven months will they search it through.</hi> Eze 39:15. <hi type="italic">And those who rove about will pass through the land; and if one sees a man’s bone, he will set up a sign by it, till the buriers of the dead bury it in the valley of the multitude of Gog.</hi> Eze 39:16. <hi type="italic">The name of a city shall also be called Hamonah (multitude). And thus will they cleanse the land.</hi> Eze 39:17. <hi type="italic">And thou, son of man, thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Say to the birds of every plumage, and to all the beasts of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come, gather together from round about to my sacrifice, which I slaughter for you, to a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, and eat flesh and drink blood.</hi> Eze 39:18. <hi type="italic">Flesh of heroes shall ye eat, and drink blood of princes of the earth; rams, lambs, and he-goats, bullocks, all fattened in Bashan.</hi> Eze 39:9. <hi type="italic">And ye shall eat fat to satiety, and drink blood to intoxication, of my sacrifice which I have slaughtered for you.</hi> Eze 39:20. <hi type="italic">And ye shall satiate yourselves at my table with horses and riders, heroes and all kinds of men of war, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah.</hi> - To show how terrible the judgment upon Gog will be, Ezekiel depicts in three special ways the total destruction of his powerful forces. In the <hi type="italic">first</hi> place, the burning of all the weapons of the fallen foe will furnish the inhabitants of the land of Israel with wood for firing for seven years, so that there will be no necessity for them to fetch fuel from the field or from the forest (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.9">Eze 39:9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.10">Eze 39:10</reference>). But Hävernick is wrong in supposing that the reason for burning the weapons is that, according to <reference osisRef="Isa.9.5">Isa 9:5</reference>, weapons of war are irreconcilable with the character of the Messianic times of peace. This is not referred to here; but the motive is the complete annihilation of the enemy, the removal of every trace of him. The prophet therefore crowds the words together for the purpose of enumerating every kind of weapon that was combustible, even to the hand-staves which men were accustomed to carry (cf. Num 22:27). The quantity of the weapons will be so great, that they will supply the Israelites with all the fuel they need for seven years. The number seven in the seven years as well as in the seven months of burying (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.11">Eze 39:11</reference>) is symbolical, stamping the overthrow as a punishment inflicted by God, the completion of a divine judgment. <div eID="gen15201" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15202" type="x-p"/> With the gathering of the weapons for burning there is associated the plundering of the fallen foe (<hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Ezek.39.10">Eze 39:10</reference></hi>), by which the Israelites do to the enemy what he intended to do to them (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.12">Eze 38:12</reference>), and the people of God obtain possession of the wealth of their foes (cf. <reference osisRef="Jer.30.16">Jer 30:16</reference>). In the <hi type="italic">second</hi> place, God will assign a large burying-place for the army of Gog in a valley of Israel, which is to be named in consequence “the multitude of Gog;” just as a city in that region will also be called <hi type="italic">Hamonah</hi> from this event. The Israelites will bury the fallen of Gog there for seven months long, and after the expiration of that time they will have the land explored by men specially appointed for the purpose, and bones that may still have been left unburied will be sought out, and they will have them interred by buriers of the dead, that the land may be thoroughly cleansed (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.11-Ezek.39.16">Eze 39:11-16</reference>). מקום שׁם, a place where there was a grave in Israel, i.e., a spot in which he might be buried in Israel. There are different opinions as to both the designation and the situation of this place. There is no foundation for the supposition that גּי העברים derives its name from the mountains of <hi type="italic">Abarim</hi> in Num 27:12 and <reference osisRef="Deut.32.49">Deu 32:49</reference> (Michaelis, Eichhorn), or that it signifies valley of the haughty ones (Ewald), or that there is an allusion to the valley mentioned in Zec 14:4 (Hitzig), or the valley of Jehoshaphat (Kliefoth). The valley cannot even have derived its name (העברים) from the עברים, who passed through the land to search out the bones of the dead that still remained unburied, and have them interred (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.14">Eze 39:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.15">Eze 39:15</reference>). For העברים cannot have any other meaning here than that which it has in the circumstantial clause which follows, where those who explored the land cannot possibly be intended, although even this clause is also obscure. The only other passage in which חסם occurs is <reference osisRef="Deut.25.4">Deu 25:4</reference>, where it signifies a muzzle, and in the Arabic it means to obstruct, or cut off; and hence, in the passage before us, probably, to stop the way. העברים are not the Scythians (Hitzig), for the word עבר is never applied to their invasion of the land, but generally the travellers who pass through the land, or more especially those who cross from Peraea to Canaan. The valley of העברים is no doubt the valley of the Jordan above the Dead Sea. The definition indicates this, viz., קדמת, on the front of the sea; not to the east of the sea, as it is generally rendered, for קדמת never has this meaning (see the comm. on <reference osisRef="Gen.2.14">Gen 2:14</reference>). By היּם we cannot understand “the Mediterranean,”as the majority of the commentators have done, as there would then be no meaning in the words, since the whole of the land of Israel was situated to the east of the Mediterranean Sea. היּם is the Dead Sea, generally called היּם הקּדמוני (<reference osisRef="Ezek.47.18">Eze 47:18</reference>); and קדמת, “on the front side of the (Dead) Sea,” as looked at from Jerusalem, the central point of the land, is probably the valley of the Jordan, the principal crossing place from Gilead into Canaan proper, and the broadest part of the Jordan-valley, which was therefore well adapted to be the burial-place for the multitude of slaughtered foes. But in consequence of the army of Gog having there found its grave, this valley will in future block up the way to the travellers who desire to pass to and fro. This appears to be the meaning of the circumstantial clause. <div eID="gen15202" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15203" type="x-p"/> From the fact that Gog’s multitude is buried there, the valley itself will receive the name of <hi type="italic">Hamon-Gog</hi>. The Israelites will occupy seven months in burying them, so enormously great will be the number of the dead to be buried (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.12">Eze 39:12</reference>), and this labour will be for a name, i.e., for renown, to the whole nation. This does not mean, of course, “that it will be a source of honour to them to assist in this work;” nor is the renown to be sought in the fact, that as a privileged people, protected by God, they can possess the grave of Gog in their land (Hitzig), - a thought which is altogether remote, and perfectly foreign to Israelitish views; but the burying of Gog’s multitude of troops will be for a name to the people of Israel, inasmuch as they thereby cleanse the land and manifest their zeal to show themselves a holy people by sweeping all uncleanness away. יום is an accusative of time: on the day when I glorify myself. - <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.14">Eze 39:14</reference>, Eze 39:15. The effort made to cleanse the land perfectly from the uncleanness arising from the bones of the dead will be so great, that after the great mass of the slain have been buried in seven months, there will be men specially appointed to bury the bones of the dead that still lie scattered here and there about the land. אנשׁי תּמיד are people who have a permanent duty to discharge. The participles עברים and מקבּרים are co-ordinate, and are written together <hi type="italic">asyndetos</hi>, men who go about the land, and men who bury with those who go about. That the words are to be understood in this sense is evident from <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.15">Eze 39:15</reference>, according to which those who go about do not perform the task of burying, but simply search for bones that have been left, and put up a sign for the buriers of the dead. ראה, with the subject indefinite; if one sees a human bone, he builds (erects) a ציּוּן, or stone, by the side of it (cf. 2Ki 23:17). - Eze 39:16. A city shall also receive the name of <hi type="italic">Hamonah</hi>, i.e., multitude or tumult. To שׁם־עיר we may easily supply יהיה from the context, since this puts in the future the statement, “the name of the city is,” for which no verb was required in Hebrew. In the last words, וטהרוּ הארץ, the main thought is finally repeated and the picture brought to a close. - <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.17">Eze 39:17</reference>-20. In the <hi type="italic">third</hi> place, God will provide the birds of prey and beasts of prey with an abundant meal from this slaughter. This cannot be understood as signifying that only what remain of the corpses, and have not been cleared away in the manner depicted in <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.11-Ezek.39.16">Eze 39:11-16</reference>, will become the prey of wild beasts; but the beasts of prey will make their meal of the corpses before it is possible to bury them, since the burying cannot be effected immediately or all at once. - The several features in the picture, of the manner in which the enemies are to be destroyed till the last trace of them is gone, are not arranged in chronological order, but according to the subject-matter; and the thought that the slaughtered foes are to become the prey of wild beasts is mentioned last as being the more striking, because it is in this that their ignominious destruction culminates. To give due prominence to this thought, the birds and beasts of prey are summoned by God to gather together to the meal prepared for them. The picture given of it as a sacrificial meal is based upon <reference osisRef="Isa.34.6">Isa 34:6</reference> and Jer 46:10. In harmony with this picture the slaughtered foes are designated as fattened sacrificial beasts, rams, lambs, he-goats, bullocks; on which Grotius has correctly remarked, that “these names of animals, which were generally employed in the sacrifices, are to be understood as signifying different orders of men, chiefs, generals, soldiers, as the Chaldee also observes.”
entries.17854a005c71e63e2860fe4b06765d17253c7c50: <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.21-Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:21-29</reference> <div eID="gen15203" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">The Result of this Judgment, and the Concluding Promise</title> <div sID="gen15204" type="x-p"/> Eze 39:21. T<hi type="italic">hen will I display my glory among the nations, and all nations shall see my judgment which I shall execute, and my hand which I shall lay upon them.</hi> Eze 39:22. <hi type="italic">And the house of Israel shall know that I am Jehovah their God from this day and forward.</hi> Eze 39:23. <hi type="italic">And the nations shall know that because of their wickedness the house of Israel went into captivity; because they have been unfaithful toward me, I hid my face from them, and gave them into the hand of their oppressors, so that they all fell by the sword.</hi> Eze 39:24. <hi type="italic">According to their uncleanness, and according to their transgressions, I dealt with them, and hid my face from them.</hi> Eze 39:25. <hi type="italic">Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Now will I bring back the captivity of Jacob, and have pity upon all the house of Israel, and be jealous for my holy name.</hi> Eze 39:26. <hi type="italic">Then will they bear their reproach and all their faithlessness which they have committed toward me when they dwell in their land in security, and no one alarms them;</hi> Eze 39:27. <hi type="italic">When I bring them back out of the nations, and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, and sanctify myself upon them before the eyes of the many nations.</hi> Eze 39:28. <hi type="italic">And they will know that I, Jehovah, am their God, when I have driven them out to the nations, and then bring them together again into their land, and leave none of them there any more.</hi> Eze 39:29. <hi type="italic">And I will not hide my face from them any more, because I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah.</hi> - The terrible judgment upon Gog will have this twofold effect as a revelation of the glory of God - <hi type="italic">first</hi>, Israel will know that the Lord is, and will always continue to be, its God (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.22">Eze 39:22</reference>); <hi type="italic">secondly</hi>, the heathen will know that He gave Israel into their power, and thrust it out of its own land, not from weakness, but to punish it for its faithless apostasy (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.23">Eze 39:23</reference> and <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.24">Eze 39:24</reference>; compare Eze 36:17.). עשׂה אתם (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.24">Eze 39:24</reference>), as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.7.27">Eze 7:27</reference>, etc. But because this was the purpose of the Lord with His judgments, He will now bring back the captives of Israel, and have compassion upon all His people. This turn of the prophecy in <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.25">Eze 39:25</reference> serves to introduce the promise to Israel with which the prophecy concerning Gog and the whole series of prophecies, contained in <reference osisRef="Ezek.35.1">Eze 35:1</reference> onwards, are brought to a close (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.25-Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:25-29</reference>). This promise reverts in 'עתּה אשׁיב וגו to the prophet’s own time, to which Ezekiel had already gone back by mentioning the carrying away of Israel in <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.23">Eze 39:23</reference> and Eze 39:24. The restoration of the captives of Jacob commences with the liberation of Israel from the Babylonian exile, but is not to be restricted to this. It embraces all the deliverances which Israel will experience from the termination of the Babylonian exile till its final gathering out of the nations on the conversion of the remnant which is still hardened and scattered. לכן, therefore, sc. because God will prove Himself to be holy in the sight of the heathen nations by means of the judgment, and will make known to them that He has punished Israel solely on account of its sins, and therefore will He restore His people and renew it by His Spirit (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:29</reference>). - In what the jealousy of God for His holy name consists is evident from v.7, and still more plainly from <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.22-Ezek.36.23">Eze 36:22-23</reference>, namely, in the fact that by means of the judgment He manifests Himself as the holy God. ונשׂוּ is not to be altered into ונשׁוּ, “they will forget,” as Dathe and Hitzig propose, but is a defective spelling for ונשׂאוּ (like מלוּ for מלאוּ in <reference osisRef="Ezek.28.16">Eze 28:16</reference>): they will bear their reproach. The thought is the same as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.54">Eze 16:54</reference> and <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.61">Eze 16:61</reference>, where the bearing of reproach is explained as signifying their being ashamed of their sins and their consequences, and feeling disgust thereat. They will feel this shame when the Lord grants them lasting peace in their own land. Raschi has correctly explained it thus: “When I shall have done them good, and not rewarded them as their iniquity deserved, they will be filled with shame, so that they will not dare to lift up their face.” - <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.27">Eze 39:27</reference> is only a further expansion of <hi type="italic"><reference osisRef="Ezek.39.26">Eze 39:26</reference></hi>. For the fact itself, compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.23-Ezek.36.24">Eze 36:23-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.41">Eze 20:41</reference>, etc. And not only will Israel then be ashamed of its sins, but (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.28">Eze 39:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:29</reference>) it will also know that Jehovah is its God from henceforth and for ever, as was affirmed in <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.22">Eze 39:22</reference>, when He shall fully restore to their own land the people that was thrust into exile, and withdraw His favour from it no more, because He has poured out His Spirit upon it, and thereby perfectly sanctified it as His own people (cf. <reference osisRef="Ezek.36.27">Eze 36:27</reference>). <div eID="gen15204" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15205" type="x-p"/> The promise with which the prophecy concerning the destruction of Gog is brought to a close, namely, that in this judgment all nations shall see the glory of God, and all Israel shall know that henceforth Jehovah will be their God, and will no more hide His face from them, serves to confirm the substance of the threat of punishment; inasmuch as it also teaches that, in the destruction of Gog and his gathering of peoples, the last attack of the heathen world-power upon the kingdom of God will be judged and overthrown, so that from that time forth the people of God will no more have to fear a foe who can disturb its peace and its blessedness in the everlasting possession of the inheritance given to it by the Lord. Gog is not only depicted as the last foe, whom the Lord Himself entices for the purpose of destroying him by miracles of His almighty power (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.3-Ezek.38.4">Eze 38:3-4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.19-Ezek.38.22">Eze 38:19-22</reference>), by the fact that his appearance is assigned to the end of the times, when all Israel is gathered out of the nations and brought back out of the lands, and dwells in secure repose in the open and unfortified towns of its own land (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.8">Eze 38:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.11-Ezek.38.12">Eze 38:11-12</reference>); but this may also be inferred from the fact that the gathering of peoples led by Gog against Israel belongs to the heathen nations living on the borders of the known world,since this points to a time when not only will the ancient foes of the kingdom of God, whose destruction was predicted in Ezekiel 25-32, have departed from the stage of history and perished, but the boundaries of Israel will also stretch far beyond the limits of Palestine, to the vicinity of these hordes of peoples at the remotest extremities on the north, the east, and the south of the globe. - So much may be gathered from the contents of our prophecy in relation to its historical fulfilment. But in order to determine with greater precision what is the heathen power thus rising up in Gog of Magog against the kingdom of God, we mut take into consideration the passage in the Apocalypse (<reference osisRef="Rev.20.8">Rev 20:8</reference> and <reference osisRef="Rev.20.9">Rev 20:9</reference>), where our prophecy is resumed. Into this, however, we will not further enter till after the exposition of Ezekiel 40-48, when we shall take up the question as to the historical realization of the new temple and kingdom of God which Ezekiel saw.  <chapter eID="Ezek.39"/> <div eID="gen15205" type="x-p"/>

Other tell us, 'tis a certain number for an uncertain, others that 'tis somewhat a proverbi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />al speech, they shall have enough by the spoil of the Enemy to make them and keep them warm, much as we sometimes say of one well provided, he is a warm Gentleman, and some others tell us, 'tis an expression of the Jews, who love to use this num<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber in extraordinary cases, though they intend not precisely the same, as we say of a thing delay'd 'twill be seven years ere it come, or of a thing that will serve us a good while, 'twill last seven years. They shall be sufficient, and in such a Countrey, where the need of fire is much less then with us, it will not seem very incredible, that the warlike Utensils of so numerous an Army might be enough to furnish them with fewel for so many years, or more.</ns0:note> seven years.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 So <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>And</ns0:hi> they shall not, &c.</ns0:note> that they shall <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">This, as noted before, taken Potentially, or speaking what they might, not what they eventually should do, such store of fuel from the Weapons, and Utensils of War left by these <ns0:hi>Gogites,</ns0:hi> that the Jews will not need to go to the Forests to cut down Wood. Or else <ns0:hi>comparatively,</ns0:hi> as some will, what they shall need to fetch from the Forests shall be nothing in comparison to what they were wont to fetch.</ns0:note> take no wood out of the field, neither cut down <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> out of the for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ests; for they shall <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">They may if they will, 'tis not <ns0:hi>preceptive,</ns0:hi> to make it duty, nor doth it necessarily determin, that they must, but there were and would be for all that time, who would be burning these Weapons, and save the labour and cost of buying, and fetching Wood, and these, who should do this, I would look for among the poorer sort.</ns0:note> burn the weapons with fire: and they shall spoil <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Strip the dead, rifle their Waggons, and Tents, searching what they may find of value and use, in which tis likely, the poor among the Jews would be earliest, and most diligent.</ns0:note> those that spoiled <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The Army of <ns0:hi>Gog,</ns0:hi> and his Followers.</ns0:note> them, and rob <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">'Twas not Theft or Robbery in the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> to do this, though 'twas Rob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bery in <ns0:hi>Gog</ns0:hi> and his Company to spoil the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> but for <ns0:hi>decorum</ns0:hi> of the phrase, the Prophet useth the same word in both cases.</ns0:note> those that robbed them, saith the Lord GOD.</ns0:p>

                  </ns0:note> men of continual employment, passing <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">To go up and down over the whole Land, for many of <ns0:hi>Gogs</ns0:hi> wounded, flying Souldiers died in Thickets, and by corners into which they crept, when they could go no farther.</ns0:note> through the land to bury with the passengers <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Whose assistance they would desire of courtesie, or command by order, and that with reason, all this care and la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour for burying the dead tending to their good, that they might unoffended travel whether they were going.</ns0:note> those that remain <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Unbu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried by the publick labour of the house of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> during the seven moneths.</ns0:note> upon the face of the earth to cleanse <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">A legal cleansing, if refered to <ns0:hi>Antio<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="23">23 And the heathen shall know, that the house of Israel went into captivity for their ini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quity <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The sottish heathen thought meanly of the God of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and reckoned they came into Captivity, because the People of some greater God had by the power of their God, prevailed against <ns0:hi>Israels</ns0:hi> God, and his People, but by this overthrow given to <ns0:hi>Gog,</ns0:hi> they shall see 'twas not impotence in <ns0:hi>Israels</ns0:hi> God, but iniquity in <ns0:hi>Israels</ns0:hi> People, that brought them into Captivity.</ns0:note>: because they trespassed <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Committed sin perversly, continually and with an high hand.</ns0:note> against me, therefore hid I my face <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Withdrew my favour, would no more regard them, and then 'twas soon a night of trouble to them.</ns0:note> from them, and gave them into the hand <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Into the power of their Enemy which could not have hurt <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> if <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> had not first forsaken his God but then God forsook them.</ns0:note> of their enemies: so fell <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">When God withdrew his defence, as fenceless, they fell under the Sword of the Enemy, for 'tis he, that subdueth enemies, and giveth victory.</ns0:note> they all by the sword.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="25">25 Therefore <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Since my Name, my Power and Justice are vindicated, and the heathen see 'twas <ns0:hi>Israels</ns0:hi> iniquity brought them into captivi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, and <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> knows this too,</ns0:note> thus saith the Lord GOD; Now <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">From this time of <ns0:hi>Gogs</ns0:hi> over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />throw.</ns0:note> will I bring again the captivity of Ja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cob <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The seed of <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> here called by their Fathers name.</ns0:note>, and have mercy <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">This reducing Captive <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> is meer mercy; its very true, by sin they deserved to be made Captives, and 'tis as true, they never did, or could deserve a deliverance from Captivity, 'twas not extremity of justice, that so punisht, but 'twas the riches of mercy that so pardon'd, and redeemed.</ns0:note> upon the whole <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">On the ten Tribes with the two.</ns0:note> house of Israel, and will be jealous for my holy name.<ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">And all this in zeal for my holy name, by which I am engaged to be their God.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="26">26 After <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">They have long suffered, and now shall suffer no longer: for it is enough my People know, and the heathen know, that I am the Lord.</ns0:note> that they have born their shame <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Reproach for their sins cast on then by the heathen with great reflections on their God, this was part of the punishment of them all, and the greatest grief to the best among them, that their God was reproacht.</ns0:note>, and all their trespasses <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of those trespasses, whereby they sinned against God, which this Prophet plainly and frequently chargeth them with.</ns0:note>, whereby they have trespassed against me, when they dwelt safely <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">And this done amidst that prosperity, and safety, which should have obliged them to love and obedience, but when they were safe at home, they sinned as if danger would never over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />take them.</ns0:note> in their land, and none made <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> afraid <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">No Enemy to endanger and alarm them, strange ingratitude to cast off the fear of God, and his Law, when he had set them free from the fear of Enemies.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
